sections.h2: What do Roseville sellers deal with first?
sections.html:
Roseville is a compact, densely built Macomb County city. Its clearest local rule for sellers covers rental houses, which carry a city Certificate of Compliance and an ownership transfer fee. Every sale, rental or not, also runs through the Macomb County Register of Deeds and the city assessor.

Downtown Detroit lies 13 to 14 miles southwest. Roseville became a village in 1926 and a city in 1958, when the village joined the remainder of Erin Township. A population that tripled between 1950 and 1960 suggests that much of the housing stock dates from that era, so a walk-through before listing shows you what an inspector is likely to flag.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Roseville's streets and shopping centers?
sections.html:
The first permanent post office opened in 1840 and gave the place its name. In 1919 Michigan's first commercial airport, Packard Field, opened at Gratiot Avenue and Frazho Road, and the site later became the Eastgate Shopping Center in the 1950s. The municipal building at Gratiot and Meier Road went up in 1929 to replace the older Erin Township building near 11 Mile Road.

City government is council-manager, with voters electing six council members, a mayor, a clerk and a treasurer for staggered four-year terms. Roseville shares the 39th Judicial District with Fraser. If a buyer asks where legal and court business is handled, the district court is the starting point, and city hall at 29777 Gratiot Avenue handles bills and permits.

sections.h2: How did Roseville's population rise and fall?
sections.html:
The 1950s were a boom: the count jumped from 15,816 to 50,195 by 1960, then peaked at 60,529 in 1970. Since 1980 it has drifted between about 47,000 and 54,000.

By July 1, 2025 the estimate had slipped to 46,863, a drop of 1.8 percent. Squeezed into 9.84 square miles, that is roughly 4,850 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What does the Census report about Roseville homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 survey puts a typical Roseville owner-occupied home at $155,800, and 65.6 percent of homes are lived in by owners. Monthly ownership costs run $1,246 with a mortgage and $536 without.

  • Typical rent is $1,233 a month, close to the cost for owners who carry a mortgage.
  • The city has 21,226 households, 2.21 people each, with a typical income of $62,182.
  • Very few move in a year: 90.8 percent had the same address twelve months earlier.
  • Four-year degrees are held by 15.5 percent of adults over 25, and the poverty rate is 12.5 percent.

Use sold prices from your own street, rather than county averages, when you settle on an asking price.

sections.h2: How do roads and schools shape Roseville buying decisions?
sections.html:
Two freeways and two state routes make Roseville an easy commuter base. I-696, the Walter P. Reuther Freeway, crosses the middle from east to west, and I-94 runs along part of the border with St. Clair Shores. Gratiot Avenue (M-3) splits the city on its way from Detroit to Mount Clemens, while Groesbeck Highway (M-97) skirts the west side. Workers average 25.7 minutes getting to their jobs.

Neighbors are St. Clair Shores to the east, Eastpointe to the south, Warren to the west, and Fraser and Clinton Township to the north. The county seat of Mount Clemens is about 7 miles northeast.

Two districts teach children here. Roseville Community Schools operate seven elementary schools, two middle schools and a high school, and Fraser Public Schools runs two elementary schools inside the city limits. Conner Creek Academy East is a charter school in town. For shopping, Macomb Mall has anchored the area since 1964, west of Gratiot.

sections.h2: What does Roseville require of a rental house?
sections.html:
The city's Non-Owner Occupied Housing Ordinance governs rentals, and a unit that passes inspection earns a Certificate of Compliance. Once the owner submits an application and payment, the rental division calls to schedule the inspection.

  • Initial inspection and first reinspection: $150 for a single family house or duplex, $100 for apartments and condominiums.
  • Each additional unit at the same location, registered with the first: $50.
  • Lockout fee: $25.
  • Transfer of ownership: $25 for the first unit and $10 for each additional unit.

The city charges that ownership transfer fee on registered rentals, so ask the rental division who files the update and when. Give a buyer who plans to keep tenants your most recent Certificate of Compliance. You can reach the rental division at rentals@roseville-mi.gov, and it can tell you whether your address still needs a registration after the sale.

sections.h2: What do the buyer and seller file with Roseville assessing?
sections.html:
Roseville expects a Property Transfer Affidavit from the buyer within 45 days, and each late day costs $5 up to $200. At closing the buyer also signs the exemption form that saves 18 mills of school operating tax.

Sellers hand in a Request to Rescind Principal Residence at the Assessing Office, which clears the way for an exemption on the next home. From May onward the assessing staff inspect parcels that sold or have active building permits.

The assessor values property at half of its market value. Taxable value is allowed to rise each year only by the lesser of inflation and 5 percent, until a sale or physical change resets it. Owners who disagree must appeal by appointment or in writing before the March Board of Review closes.

sections.h2: What fees apply when a Roseville deed is filed in Macomb County?
sections.html:
Macomb charges the same $30 whether a deed runs two pages or twenty, with $3 more per extra instrument a document releases. Four dollars of the $30 is passed to a state survey fund.

Before a warranty deed or land contract is accepted, the treasurer stamps a tax certificate, priced at $5 for the first five legal descriptions. The recording office is on North Main Street in Mount Clemens.

On Macomb's schedule the state portion is the price times 0.0075 and the county portion is the price times 0.0011. Sellers are the ones who pay. Conveyances to a child or grandchild and foreclosure transfers are on the county's exemption list, and the deed has to say which exemption applies.

sections.h2: How do Roseville tax deadlines and penalties work?
sections.html:
Bills go out in July and December. Summer payments are due by August 31 and pick up a penalty of 1 percent per month from September 1; winter payments are due by February 28. Anything still open on March 1 is handed to the Macomb County Treasurer.

Homeowners who are 62 or older and earn under $40,000 can postpone the summer bill to February 28 for 1 percent monthly interest, if they file by September 15. Seniors can also get free help with state homestead credits.

A duplicate bill costs $2 a parcel. If you close soon after a due date, ask the title company to confirm payment so the buyer does not inherit a penalty.

faqs.q: Is there a Roseville fee when a rental changes hands?
faqs.a: Yes: $25 for the first unit and $10 for each added unit, according to the city's rental fee list.

faqs.q: What does filing a Roseville deed with Macomb County cost?
faqs.a: A flat $30, whatever the page count, with $4 going to the state survey fund. Warranty deeds also need a $5 tax certificate.

faqs.q: Which dates matter for Roseville property tax bills?
faqs.a: August 31 for summer, February 28 for winter, and March 1 when unpaid balances move to the Macomb County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Roseville sale?
faqs.a: The seller, at the 0.0075 state and 0.0011 county multipliers on Macomb's schedule.

faqs.q: How do I end my homestead exemption in Roseville?
faqs.a: File the city's Request to Rescind Principal Residence form with the Assessing Office, then claim the exemption on your next home.
